explain.say: A cantilever is a beam fixed at one end and sticking out into the air, like a diving board. A cantilever bridge uses pairs of them reaching out from each tower.

explain.say: Each tower carries two arms pointing in opposite directions, like a person holding out both arms. The arms balance each other around the tower, so it is pushed straight down instead of being toppled.

explain.say: The arms from neighbouring towers do not quite meet. A lighter suspended span hangs between their tips, and its weight is shared by the two arm ends.

explain.say: Because each side balances, builders can extend the arms outward piece by piece from the tower, with no supports in the water below. The Forth Bridge in Scotland, opened in 1890, was built this way.

faq.a: A cantilever is a beam supported at only one end, like a diving board or a balcony. Its top edge is stretched and its bottom edge squeezed, the opposite of a beam supported at both ends.

faq.q: How does a cantilever bridge work?
faq.a: Pairs of cantilever arms reach out from each tower and balance each other. A short suspended span links the tips of arms from neighbouring towers.
asks: How do cantilever bridges stay up?

faq.q: Why do the cantilever arms need to balance?
faq.a: If one arm had a much bigger turning effect, the tower would be twisted and could topple. Balancing weight times distance on each side means the tower is only pushed straight down.
asks: What keeps a cantilever bridge from tipping?

faq.a: It is a shorter beam hung between the tips of two cantilever arms to close the gap. It can be light because the arms do most of the reaching.
It can be built outward from the towers without scaffolding in deep or busy water, and it is very stiff, which suited heavy railway trains.
asks: Why was the Forth Bridge a cantilever?

facts: The Forth Bridge in Scotland opened in 1890 and has two main spans of about 521 metres each.
The Quebec Bridge in Canada, completed in 1917, still has the longest cantilever span in the world, 549 metres.

quiz.say: In a model cantilever, one arm weighs 6 units and acts 3 units from the tower. Which arm on the other side balances it?
quiz.why: Turning effect is weight times distance: 6 times 3 is 18, and 9 times 2 is also 18.

wrong.1: 6 times 2 is only 12, so the first side would tip down.
wrong.2: 3 times 3 is only 9, half of what is needed.
